title: Spatio-temporal coherent molding and retrieval of pulsed signals in optical waveguides
authors: Nika Durishvili, Ramaz Khomeriki, Vakhtang Jandieri, Douglas H. Werner, Daniel Erni, Jamal Berakdar
abstract: Optical waveguides are key elements for high fidelity, long distance optical communications. Coupled waveguide arrays allow for higher information density, steerting the propagation direction, and for encoding information. However, due to the mixing of relative phases for short pulses containing multiple waveguide-mode frequencies, a process for retrieving an encoded input state once these signals undergo coherent propagation remains elusive. A concept is presented to extract with high fidelity the phase-encrypted input signal from spatio-temporal propagated states. As a realization, an array of coupled waveguides is suggested with the retrieval mechanism being realized by local phase shifts that comply with the identified retrieval concept. Three dimensional full-wave electromagnetic simulations for broadband optical signals in coupled dielectric waveguides confirm the validity of the scheme and the high fidelity of information retrieval pointing to potential applications, for instance in ultrafast coherent coding and decoding of information imprinted on pulse sequences.
summary: This paper presents a method to retrieve an input optical signal that has been encoded and propagated through a complex, coupled waveguide array. The retrieval mechanism relies on introducing a precise, engineered phase shift at the output section (decoder). Simulations confirm that this approach allows for high-fidelity signal reconstruction, suggesting applications in ultrafast coherent information processing.
main_problem: The core challenge is retrieving a phase-encrypted input optical signal with high fidelity after it has undergone complex, coherent propagation through an array of coupled waveguides.
main_result: The proposed scheme successfully demonstrates the retrieval of the input broadband signal using a localized phase-shifting mechanism in the decoder section of the waveguide array.
method: The retrieval is achieved by applying a specific, engineered phase shift ($\pi$ shift in odd waveguides) at the decoder entrance, which theoretically causes a coherent inversion of the propagation evolution.
model_or_system: The system utilizes an array of coupled dielectric waveguides, modeled by a discrete Schrödinger-type equation describing the evolution of the electric field components along the propagation direction (z).
key_observables: Global fidelity ($F_{gl}$) and phase fidelity ($F_{ph}$) are used to quantify the success of signal retrieval, alongside cross-sectional electric field distributions.
important_parameters: Key parameters include coupling strengths ($J_\ell$), dielectric permittivities ($\epsilon_{r1}, \epsilon_{sr}$), and the pulse characteristics ($\lambda = 1.55 \mu	ext{m}$, 18 fs duration).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to implement precise, engineered phase shifts at the decoder and assumes the weak-coupling regime for the waveguide array.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup of the coder and decoder, the evolution of the electric field magnitude through the system, and plots showing the fidelity versus propagation distance.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical problem in coupled waveguides, develops the theoretical framework using coupled-mode equations, proposes the phase-shifting retrieval concept, and validates the scheme using full-wave electromagnetic simulations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses coherent control and signal processing in structured photonic media, which has strong overlap with quantum optics and open quantum system dynamics, particularly regarding time-reversal concepts.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. (a) Schematics for coding (from z = z0 to z = lc) and decoding (from z = lt to z = ld) device. (b) The coder and decoder are composed of the coupled waveguides. The pulses are injected in independent waveguides at z < z0. Coupling causes the power to randomly distribute at z = lc, encrypting the input signal. The pulses are transferred to the decoder at z = lt via independent transmission lines. At z = lt the signal is decoded according to the scheme in the manuscript.
